name: The Masters of the Renaissance
description: From Giotto's solid figures to Michelangelo's ceiling and El Greco's last works: the painters, sculptors and architects of the Renaissance in Italy and the north, and what they made.

checkpoints.name: Before the rebirth
checkpoints.note: In Tuscany, Giotto paints people with weight and feeling, and a century later Florence is ready to look back at Rome and Greece for ideas.

checkpoints.name: Florence leads
checkpoints.note: Brunelleschi raises the great dome over Florence and works out linear perspective, and Donatello casts a bronze David. In the north Jan van Eyck finishes the Ghent Altarpiece in 1432, with oil paint of a new richness and detail.

checkpoints.name: The high Renaissance
checkpoints.note: Botticelli paints The Birth of Venus, Leonardo The Last Supper and the Mona Lisa, and Michelangelo carves the David and paints the Sistine ceiling, while Raphael paints The School of Athens. In the north Durer brings the new art to woodcut and engraving, and Bosch paints The Garden of Earthly Delights.

checkpoints.name: Venice and beyond
checkpoints.note: Titian's colour rules Venice, Palladio designs villas, Bruegel paints village life in the Low Countries and Sinan builds mosques for the Ottomans. El Greco, trained in Venice and Rome, carries the late style to Spain and works in Toledo until 1614.
